extra.message: User-controlled input from the 'name' query parameter is interpolated into 'content' (line 38) and then passed to Jinja2 Template(content).render(). Because the user input becomes part of the template source itself, an attacker can inject template expressions (e.g. /?name={{7*6}} or {{config}}/{{self.__init__.__globals__}}) leading to Server-Side Template Injection and ultimately remote code execution. The commented-out test on lines 39-41 of test_main.py confirms this is the intended attack path.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 'name' query parameter is reflected directly into an HTML response via an f-string without any output encoding/escaping, and the result is returned as an HTMLResponse. An attacker can supply HTML/JavaScript (e.g. /?name=<script>alert(1)</script>) which will be executed in the victim's browser, resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: A secret token is hardcoded directly in the source code as SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN = '5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n'. Hardcoded credentials checked into source control are exposed to anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated without a code change. The value should be loaded from an environment variable / secrets manager instead.

A secret value is hardcoded directly in source code as SUPER_SECRET_NAME = 'John Ripper'. This 'secret' is committed to the repository and used as a default that is reflected back to users in the response, exposing internal configuration data. It should be loaded from an environment variable instead of being hardcoded.

The FastAPI application is initialized with debug=config.DEBUG, where DEBUG is driven by an environment variable (and set to True in .env_temp). Running with debug enabled in production exposes detailed stack traces and internal application state to clients, which can leak sensitive information and aid attackers.
